records.name: Ireland
records.summary_text:
Ireland is a calm, comfortable destination for transgender visitors. It was one of the first countries to introduce legal gender recognition by self-declaration — the 2015 Gender Recognition Act lets adults change their legal gender without medical requirements — and bathroom use is unrestricted. A hate-crime law covering sexual orientation and gender identity took effect at the end of 2024, equality law bans discrimination in employment, housing and services, and marriage equality was approved by referendum in 2015.

records.name: Belgium
records.summary_text:
Belgium is a top-tier destination for transgender visitors. Legal gender and name change by self-declaration has been available since 2018, anti-discrimination law covers gender identity and expression across employment, housing and services, hate crime and hate speech are both criminalised for gender identity, and transphobia is a separately tracked hate-crime motive. Belgium also passed Europe's first femicide law (2023), with protections for gender minorities.
